svg.title: Reading the MgSO₄–H₂O enthalpy–concentration chart (MSH Fig. 27.4)
svg.text: Reading the MgSO₄–H₂O enthalpy–concentration chart (MSH Fig. 27.4)
Datum: liquid water at 32 °F. Isotherms in the one-phase field; tie lines in the two-phase areas
Start: 32.5 % solution at 120 °F. Go up from x = 0.325 to the 120 °F isotherm: the point is still in the
one-phase (undersaturated) field, above the solubility line a-b-c-d. 3 → 4 across: H₁ = −33.0 Btu/lb.
After cooling to 70 °F the magma lies on the 70 °F tie line in area cihb (MgSO₄·7H₂O + mother liquor),
at the same overall x = 0.325. 7 → 8 across: H₂ = −78.4 Btu/lb.
The tie-line ends give the phases: mother liquor x = 0.259 and crystals MgSO₄·7H₂O x = 0.488 (lever rule).
Approximate redraw of MSH Fig. 27.4 (key points digitized, isotherms straight); in the exam read the printed chart.
